scope: Proposition 8.1 (Pole-sheaf stabilization on the invariant Iitaka model) of the manuscript “Cohomological transfer and equivariant anticanonical sections” (preprints/Cohomological-transfer-and-equivariant-anticanonical-sections-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 068 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6e231fa726d0f6b6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let V → W → X, g : W → Y , f : V → Y , and DV = π∗(−KX) be the normal equidimensional model and smooth resolution in the preceding invariant Iitaka construction. Put E = KV/X. Retain its invariant adjoint rank-one condition (23) and its curvature-kernel inclusion, and write bDV = G + f∗Q after vertical normalization, with G pulled back from the normal model and omitting a divisorial lift of each base prime. Then the increasing invariant pole sheaves Pk = (f∗OV (E +kG))T , viewed as rational functions through sEsk G, stabilize. The line Q is nef and G contains no entire fiber. These conclusions give a second proof that the fiberwise maximum defines a positive continuous metric.
